scope: P1 durable/public/resource/effect source and selected tests/examples. Root owns joined services/frontend/infrastructure; other agents own P2/P3. Inventory-only files are explicitly identified. This is not exhaustive execution or production qualification.

summary.judgment: Reviewed business authority and recovery deliberately remain stronger than conversational Academy examples. No scope/consent/lease/external-effect authority bypass was confirmed in the reviewed paths. A real diagnostic-containment defect was reproduced and fixed; post-dispatch pacing remains known open.

findings.title: Logger failures and diagnostic getters could replace a successful inquiry result or primary error

evidence.claim: Ordinary logging failures are now contained
Successful persistence result exists before completed event
Legacy inquiry getter now preserves the primary failure

failure_path: An application logger raises on managed_worker_completed after lifecycle.finish_success returned. Previously run_one raised the logger OSError instead of returning the successful result.
If the primary exception has a raising code property, old managed-worker diagnostic selection replaced the exception. InquiryWorker had the same variant for ExecutionError/MigrationError subclasses.
Eight older _event helpers allowed logger failures to escape, unlike newer mutation/effects/leases/work helpers.

reproduction.before: First three new test methods: 10 errors (eight event-helper subtests plus two managed paths). Added legacy inquiry getter method separately failed: LookupError replaced original ExecutionError.
reproduction.after: Entire tests.test_inquiry_worker passes 19/19 in 0.391 seconds. New methods also verify KeyboardInterrupt propagation.

findings.fix: Contain ordinary Exception only in eight event helpers; protect both inquiry-worker error-code lookups and retain bare re-raise/fixed finite fallback. No transaction, consent, cancellation, dispatch, retry, lease, schema or public API change.
findings.proof_boundary: Public managed-worker regression uses a controlled lifecycle adapter whose finish_success returns its completed result. It proves caller-visible control flow, not a fresh PostgreSQL commit/crash or media/provider gate.

findings.title: v5 persisted pacing excludes dependency outages after dispatch reservation

evidence.claim: Unavailable lookup after a possible call is re-raised
Due time only written for pre-dispatch dependency_unavailable
Repeated recovered claims consume finite attempt budget
Selector due filter applies only to pending effects

failure_path: Cooperating mutation reserves dispatch, then apply and reconciliation lookup are unavailable. Effect remains possibly dispatched.
Recovery claims a new attempt; another unavailable lookup is re-raised without persisted due pacing. Worker poll cadence can repeatedly consume attempts.
A temporary outage can exhaust attempts into terminal uncertainty. Stable identity/uncertainty safety remains; this is a useful-progress/pacing limitation, never permission to retry with another key.
findings.next_step: Separate design and actual PostgreSQL outage/recovery test for paced reconciliation of possible effects. Do not fold this into the diagnostic fix or claim fixed.

checked_invariants.claim: Accepted-work replay compares original immutable payload before new-work expiry/caps; writes sample DB time after admission lock.
checked_invariants.test_body_read: tests/postgres/pg_readonly_work_cases.py selected assertions not freshly executed

checked_invariants.claim: Worker lease guards match scope/task/owner/epoch and expiry after locks; renewal cannot resurrect an expired grant.
A prior reservation plus cancelled/expired lookup miss yields uncertainty, not definite prevention. Known reliable success survives late cancel/deadline, subject to current lease.
Only new issuance permits invocation; eligible result truth survives later cancellation; completion snapshots caller-owned nested grant values before awaits.
Exact quote/revision confirmation, work/result eligibility and intent receipt share protected commitment; no supplier I/O occurs in that transaction.

evidence.claim: Case authority remains sole intent authority
Booking then work admission and case locks

checked_invariants.claim: Child cleanup precedes lease release; failed reap keeps ownership; cancelled waiters keep thread capacity.

academy_comparison.topic: userdata and on_exit are not crash durability
academy_comparison.judgment: P1 correctly persists before ACK instead of waiting for an exit hook. Academy itself distinguishes session memory, but its save-in-on_exit advice is insufficient for a crash guarantee.

sdk.claim: userdata is an AgentSession object field.

academy_comparison.judgment: AgentTask has an in-memory future and conversational activity. It does not replace P1 persisted attempts/results, identity reconciliation or effects.

sdk.claim: AgentTask owns asyncio.Future; complete sets that future.

academy_comparison.judgment: Explicit controller exact confirmation is a deliberate stronger project boundary. Do not expose quote/confirm/action authority as native model tools to match a tutorial.
Speech interruption and waiter timeout do not stop a durable task, thread, child or supplier request. P1 separately records cancellation and possible effects.
Room/RPC reliability does not replace original accepted key/bytes or receipt-backed recovery. Feed cursors are observations, not ACK/action authority.

project.claim: Committed result and scoped feed sequence share transaction

academy_comparison.judgment: No missing SIP, RAG, general workflow engine, dynamic model switching or automatic coroutine checkpoint was treated as a P1 bug or added. P1 standalone durable API requires no inference provider.
